title: Healthy Ageing: Measuring and Maintaining Functional Ability
abstract: Healthy ageing is defined by the World Health Organization as “the process of developing and maintaining the functional ability that enables well-being in older age” (9, 10). This definition, which underpins the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing (2021-2030), shifts the focus from the absence of disease to what people can be and do as they grow older. Functional ability reflects an individual’s intrinsic capacity, the environment, and the interaction between them. Maintaining or improving functional ability is therefore a central challenge for clinicians, researchers and practitioners in exercise and rehabilitation.

title: قيادة الجنرال هنري بيتان لمعركة فردان وسطوع نجمهُ العسكري (شباط - كانون الأول 1916)
journal: Arabian Gulf Journal of Humanities and Social Studies

title: When the crowd crashes the market: consumer complaints, informal monitoring, and stock price crash risk
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether and how consumer complaints function as an informal monitoring force affecting stock price crash risk. Design/methodology/approach This research employs a two-way fixed effects model using a matched dataset of China A-share listed firms and complaint records from the “Black Cat Complaints” platform for 2019–2023. We further corroborate the findings through endogeneity tests and heterogeneity analyses. Findings Consumer complaints increase future stock price crash risk through three channels: external triggering, by attracting media coverage and investor attention; managerial bad-news hoarding, by reducing disclosure transparency and Management Discussion and Analysis specificity; and industry spillover, by diffusing negative signals to peer firms. Further analyses show that complaint frequency predicts crash risk more strongly than claimed monetary amount, indicating that the recurrence of complaints contains more market-relevant information than their financial magnitude. Full resolution weakens but does not eliminate the complaint effect, stronger negative sentiment in complaint texts intensifies crash risk, and the effect persists into subsequent years. Originality/value This study is the first to reveal the impact of consumer complaints on stock price crash risk, clarifying how the negative signals conveyed by consumers transmit from firm level to capital market. This finding suggests that complaints contain market-unassimilated negative information predicting future crash risk, offering valuable insights for firms, investors and regulators.

journal: AIJ Journal of Technology and Design

title: Truck-Drone Collaborative Delivery Strategies in Rural Last-Mile Logistics: A Constraint Theory and Contingency Theory Review
abstract: Compared with urban regions, rural last-mile logistics faces special delivery conditions, including scattered delivery points, sparse road infrastructure and low customer demand density. Currently, truck-drone collaborative delivery has emerged as a promising solution to this issue. But strategy selection across varying rural factors remains unexplored. This review aims to examine how collaborative delivery strategies perform under distinct types of rural bottlenecks through integrating Constraint Theory and Contingency Theory. Existing literature identifies that rural last-mile delivery is primarily confronted with four bottleneck types. They include road-network-driven, demand-driven, structure-driven and hybrid. Using this classification, this study compares the performance of two-stage and integrated optimization methods across categories. Findings reveal that integrated strategies are superior under road-network and structure bottlenecks, whereas two-stage strategies suffice under demand bottlenecks. A bottleneck-oriented strategy selection framework is constructed. The review delivers a theoretical framework by integrating two management theories into collaborative delivery research, practically providing valuable decision-making guidance for logistics enterprises and policy-makers.

Too middling to stay? Perceived job complexity, occupational identity threat and career change intention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine when and how job complexity may prompt occupational reconsideration. Drawing on an identity appraisal perspective, it tests the inverted-U-shaped association between perceived job complexity and occupational identity threat, the corresponding indirect association with career change intention and the moderating role of workplace sense of power. Design/methodology/approach Two complementary studies were conducted. Study 1 analyzed from the Second European Skills and Jobs Survey data involving 43,859 employees in 29 European countries to examine the focal association. Study 2 used two-wave survey data from 434 Chinese full-time employees to test the full research model. Findings Study 1 identified an inverted-U association between job complexity and occupational identity threat in the pooled cross-national sample. Study 2 supported this pattern. Occupational identity threat peaked at intermediate complexity and was positively associated with career change intention. The indirect curvilinear association through occupational identity threat was also significant. Workplace sense of power was associated with lower threat and a more pronounced inverted-U association. Originality/value This study develops a nonlinear account of job complexity's occupational identity implications. It links everyday work design to occupational reconsideration through occupational identity threat. It also identifies workplace sense of power as a factor shaping the appraisal of complex work.

title: The contingent racial politics of municipal incorporation: fiscal diffusion and suburban segregation
abstract: Does American municipal incorporation produce racial inequality? Existing accounts emphasize either racial design or local fiscal control, but few account for variation over time. Using a 60-year panel (1962–2022) of 1,988 incorporations linked to county fiscal, demographic, and political data, this paper shows that incorporation’s racial character was contingent and temporary. Among unincorporated communities that could have incorporated, whiter ones were substantially more likely to do so during the 1990s, but not in the decades before or after. The mechanism is a fiscal externality: each incorporation withdraws tax base from its county, raising the incentive for remaining communities to follow, and because wealthier communities capture the largest benefit from exit and wealth correlated with whiteness in postwar suburbs, the process produced racially disparate outcomes when it ran through segregated suburban geography. Incorporating communities were 7.2 percentage points whiter than unincorporated communities observed in the same decade during the 1990s, with no such gap in the 1970s, 1980s, or 2010s; backlash mechanisms such as school desegregation orders, the Voting Rights Act, and racial threat fail to explain when racial selection emerged; and the pattern was self-limiting, with nearly a quarter of 2010s incorporations majority-minority. Racial disparities produced by American institutions need not arise from intentional exclusion or reactive resistance, and can emerge and dissolve through race-neutral processes operating on racially structured landscapes – which also means such disparities may persist unaddressed absent deliberate intervention.

title: Digital technologies and sustainability aid firm competitiveness
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Digital technologies are playing an increasingly major role in enhancing both the business and environmental performance of emerging economy firms. Desired outcomes can become likelier when the organization possesses and exploits strong social capital needed to build trust and relationships to inspire the sharing of knowledge and technologies that can fuel new sustainability initiatives within challenging international markets. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.
